title: PMBJP drug-code identity — RESOLVED: the finding was an artifact of the wrong PDF extraction mode
outcome: The committed catalogue drug codes are CORRECT. All 17 committed product-presentation mappings verify against the official PMBJP product list. No mapping, promotion or clinical binding was ever wrong.

what_went_wrong_in_the_investigation.summary: F5 was raised because I extracted the PMBJP list with Xpdf pdftotext -layout, which on this ruled table renders 632 of 2111 product-name cells into a separate block, orphaning them from their drug code. Comparing the catalogue against that damaged extraction produced an apparent 38.7 percent code agreement and an apparent 7 mappings pointing at different drugs.
what_went_wrong_in_the_investigation.the_actual_check: Xpdf -table extracts the same document into 2111 complete rows. Against that extraction the catalogue agrees on 2045 of 2111 rows (96.9 percent), and the remaining 66 are trailing-whitespace differences only, not different products.
what_went_wrong_in_the_investigation.corroboration: The -table ordering is alphabetical within its section (Torsemide, Valsartan, Verapamil, Warfarin 1mg, Warfarin 2mg, Zinc Sulphate), which the -layout reading breaks. The catalogue matches -table exactly, including 380 = Clarithromycin 500 mg, 740 = Clarithromycin 250 mg, 452 = Warfarin 5 mg and 2141 = Warfarin 1mg.
superseded_claims: RETRACTED: "PMBJP codes are not stable across product-list editions." Not demonstrated; the apparent instability was extraction damage.
RETRACTED: "The catalogue was built from a different, larger, unrecoverable edition." The catalogue matches the document the adapter still points at, row for row (2111 = 2111).
RETRACTED: "Our 2026-07-07 extraction paired codes to names positionally and mislabelled them." The 07-07 extraction was correct; the later -layout re-extraction was the damaged one.
RETRACTED: the corrected-code table proposing 1246->1252, 521->519, 2034->2033, 2141->2144. Those "true" codes were read off the damaged extraction. The committed codes are right.

results.mapped_product: Tramadol Prolonged Release Tablets IP 100 mg
results.source_list_product: Tramadol Prolonged Release Tablets IP 100 mg

real_defect_found_and_fixed.defect: The extraction mode was part of the data contract but was neither pinned nor checked. The janaushadhi adapter asked for -layout, which silently loses 645 rows on this document. Any rebuild performed with the currently installed Xpdf 4.00 would have produced a catalogue with wholesale-wrong drug codes, and nothing would have complained.
fixes: pdfToText now takes an explicit mode ("layout" or "table") and rejects anything else. The janaushadhi adapter requests "table", which is correct for this ruled table.

New assertJanAushadhiParseComplete compares parsed rows against the count of serial numbers present in the document — an in-document ground truth independent of name/code pairing — and throws when they differ. On the current document: -layout gives 1466 vs 2111 (throws), -table gives 2111 vs 2111 (passes).
src/cli/build.mjs asserts that completeness before accepting any janaushadhi rows, so a lossy extraction fails the build instead of silently corrupting the catalogue.
The adapter records pmbjp.provenance.json (origin, source_url, pdf_sha256, pdf_byte_count, code_space_verifiable) so a snapshot is attributable to an exact document.
npm run verify:pmbjp-mapping-codes checks every committed mapping code against a named, hashed source list and exits non-zero on any unconfirmed code.

lesson: pdftotext -layout silently mis-renders ruled tables, and a parser that only reads well-formed rows will happily return a truncated result. Any tabular extraction needs an independent in-document row count asserted against the parse, or a wrong answer looks like a clean one. That assertion now exists and would have prevented both the original risk and this false alarm.
remediation_outstanding: None blocking. The catalogue, the 17 mappings and the 7 promoted rules are verified correct.
Optional hardening: extend the same parsed-vs-ground-truth assertion to the other PDF-backed adapters (cdsco-fdc, nppa), which still use -layout without a completeness check.
